title: Heuristic paper-hunting & first-pass reading notebook — long-context inference
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for how I triage papers/blogs during an inference sprint + quick takeaways for long-context/kv/latency work. Use this as a lightweight checklist to decide whether to dig deeper, add to the reading backlog, or file an experiment ticket.

Overview (quick):
- Problem I care about: long-context LLM inference at production latencies (≤100ms per token p50 for many apps), cheaper per-token cost, and graceful degradation when context grows.
- Current hypotheses: 1) sparse/segmented KV caches with per-segment eviction outperform naive global KV for long episodic workloads; 2) small-prefix-aware quantization (mixed 4-bit + FP16 for first N tokens) preserves early-context quality; 3) micro-batching + early-decode streaming helps latency without massive throughput loss for tail queries.

Paper skim log (first-pass notes, quick verdicts):
1) "Segmented KV: efficient lookups for 1e6 token histories" (arXiv 2024-09) — quick verdict: actionable.
   - Why skimmed: exact match to hypothesis 1; claims O(log S) lookup with shard metadata.
   - Key idea: hierarchical shards + adaptive bloom filters per shard.
   - Pros: lossless retrieval when shard boundaries aligned; benchmarks show memory/time wins vs global KV for synthetic chat workloads (10k+ sessions).
   - Cons/flags: eval uses synthetic contexts with deterministic repetition; not clear on real noisy RAG traces.
   - Immediate experiment idea: run on internal RAG traces with our prefix distribution; measure hit-rate vs global KV and end-to-end p95 latency.

2) "Prefix-aware mixed quantization for streaming LLMs" (conference slides) — quick verdict: keep for deeper read.
   - Why: quantization combined with position-sensitive dequantization during decode might let us keep first 128 tokens high-precision.
   - Notes: authors use dynamic per-layer casting at runtime (FP16 for early layers/tokens, 4-bit for remainder). Claims minimal BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-hallucation change for chat benchmarks.
   - Concern: implementation complexity on our runtime (kernel swaps mid-seq). Need to evaluate engineering cost vs gain.
   - Experiment: prototype with one model shard (LlamaX-40B) on a local node; measure quality on our prompt-suite and latency overhead of dynamic casting.

3) "Micro-batching with early-token streaming" (engineering blog + open-sourced scheduler) — quick verdict: high ROI for hosted API scenarios.
   - Idea: form tiny micro-batches (<8) but start streaming as soon as first token available; use priority scheduling for low-latency sessions.
   - Observed: p50 improves a lot, throughput drop modest for bursty web traffic.
   - Implementation notes: requires changes to stream API contract + backpressure handling with websockets; good fit for hosted tier but worry for Dedicated (SLA) where reserved capacity expects deterministic throughput.
   - Quick checklist: estimate SDK changes, update streaming contract tests, spike on dev cluster.

4) "RAG hallucination probes: synthetic distractor injection" (paper) — quick verdict: useful for eval pipeline.
   - Method: inject semantically plausible distractors into retrieved docs and measure model confidence shift.
   - Fit for our Optimize product: can be adapted into an automated regression test (trigger alerts when hallucination metric crosses threshold).

Quick synthesis for product trade-offs:
- Hosting vs Dedicated: micro-batching/streaming is easiest to roll out on hosted first. Quantization/hybrid precision requires runtime kernel flexibility — likely more invasive and better targeted at Dedicated pilots first. Segmented KV seems agnostic to deployment mode but will require index rebuild across replica sets.

Unresolved questions / rough TODOs:
- How much real-world repetition exists in our customer traces? If session-level repetition is low, segmentation may not help. (TODO: run trace analysis job: JIRA-4281)
- Cost model for mixed-precision: quantify extra GPU cycles for on-the-fly demotion/promotion. (Spike: micro-bench kernels)
- Integration plan for streaming micro-batches: document SDK changes and tolerant fallback if streaming fails mid-response.

Small experiment plan (week 1 spikes):
- EXP-101: Segmented-KV quick A/B on small cluster: feed 10M real customer contexts, measure hit-rate, memory, p95 latency. Owner: Owen. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/kv-cache-exps
- EXP-102: Dynamic quant prototype on LlamaX-40B, 1 node. Measure quality on our prompt set (n=120) and token latency. Owner: me. (estimate: 3 days)
- EXP-103: Micro-batching + streaming spike in hosted sandbox. Implement priority queue and early flush path. Owner: Maya.

Notes to self (format: random quick fragments I say out loud while reading):
- "If the bloom filters are the heavy tail, can we compress them with learned sketches?"
- "Edge-case: when to fall back to global KV? maybe when shard bloom false-positive rate > 5%"
- "Need a small synthetic dataset that mirrors our retrieval noise for bench parity — can reuse RAG test harness."

Links & bookmarks (first-pass):
- Segmented KV paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01234
- Prefix-aware quant blog: https://medium.com/inference/prefix-quant-2024
- Micro-batching scheduler repo: https://github.com/open-scheduler/microstream
- Hallucination probes writeup: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05678
- Internal KV exps: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/kv-cache-exps

Ephemeral checklist before handing to squad: (tick when ready)
- [ ] Re-run trace analysis and attach sample distributions to EXP-101 ticket
- [ ] Prototype kernel timing for quant switches (basic kernels only)
- [ ] Draft SDK streaming contract changes and backward compatibility notes
- [ ] Short doc for Optimize: how hallucination probe integrates into regression alerts

Final micro-summary (one-line): prioritize segmented-KV A/B + micro-batching streaming spike this quarter; treat prefix-aware mixed quant as conditional investment after kernel-cost spike passes threshold.

End of scratchpad.

(If I revisit: convert this into a short one-pager for the infra sync and a prioritized backlog with estimated engineering days.)
